title: Console analytics retention enforcement and shard pruner
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Implement automated retention enforcement across console usage analytics to ensure PII removal, deterministic deletion, and auditable retention behavior. Scope includes: (1) retention policy enforcement layer that marks expired events and metadata; (2) background shard pruner process that permanently deletes data past retention and removes KV cache of those keys; (3) deletion audit trail and proof-of-deletion records stored in an append-only store; (4) API hooks for per-customer/tenant overrides (legal holds / extended retention) and a safe delete path for customer-initiated data deletion requests. Acceptance criteria: 1) Events older than configured retention are deleted within SLA window (default 72h of expiry) in test clusters; 2) No PII values (emails, API keys, tokens) survive retention window per sample scans; 3) Deletion audit records are queryable by Compliance and contain minimal metadata to prove deletion without reintroducing PII; 4) End-to-end e2e tests and perf benchmarks demonstrating <10% ingestion throughput regression and under 5% additional daily CPU cost for pruning; 5) Security review completed and signed off by InfoSec. Out-of-scope: retroactive reprocessing of historic analytics beyond automated pruner, and UI changes for Console (handled separately by PM/UI).
comments: 2026-02-20 — Triage: Ticket opened after PM identified gap in enforcement for per-tenant retention and lack of auditable deletion. Initial risk: medium-high due to compliance exposure for EEA customers. Assigned to Marco.

2026-02-25 — Design sync: Proposed approach documented in Confluence: /confluence/redwood/console/analytics-retention-design. Decided on two-phase rollout: mark-and-sweep with soft-delete flag + eventual physical deletion by shard pruner. Chose append-only deletion log encrypted with KMS for proofs. Trade-offs discussed: immediate physical deletion vs soft-delete window for incident recovery. Agreed to keep 72h grace window post-mark for manual recovery by SRE.

2026-03-01 — Spike results: Benchmark of shard pruning on staging (100M events) completed. Observed pruning throughput ~60k events/min on a single prune-worker; estimated needing 4 workers per region for peak load. CPU overhead acceptable; memory footprint within 1.2x baseline. Created Github spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5123

2026-03-04 — Implementation: Started implementation of retention service and background pruner. Core components: retention-policy-service (GRPC), prune-controller (Kubernetes CronJob->Job runner), deletion-audit-writer (to append-only S3 bucket + checksum manifest). Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5189 — awaiting codeowner review from @sylvia and @kevin.

2026-03-08 — Security review kickoff: Submitted security design doc and threat model to InfoSec. Key requirements: ensure deletion proofs cannot leak PII, ensure KMS key access restricted, ensure pruner runs in VPC with no public egress. Ticket REF: SEC-2245. InfoSec requested explicit test demonstrating scrubbed fields are not present in audit records.

2026-03-10 — QA notes: Added e2e tests that simulate tenant with legal_hold=true; pruner should skip that tenant. Tests added to CI pipeline with mock KMS. Observed flakey test related to timezones — fixed by normalizing timestamps to UTC in tests. Added test coverage for email/token regex scrubbing prior to audit logging.

2026-03-12 — Implementation update: Addressed codeowner feedback (reworked backoff/retry logic, added metrics emissions for pruner progress). Merged pruning worker changes into canary branch. Next: deploy canary to staging, run full-day retention sweep, run validation scripts to assert zero PII in audit store.

Follow-ups planned: (a) PM to coordinate Console UI for showing retention settings and legal hold; (b) Ops to add runbook for manual recovery within grace window; (c) Post-mortem & run-rate cost estimate for ongoing prune workers to be included in monthly ops budget review.
